function.name: edit

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

function.name: write
function.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# preflight_check.sh - verify the user records database is readable before an export.
# Records that the check ran (state/preflight_done) and reports whether the database
# can be opened and queried. Exits non-zero when the database is unusable.
set -u

DB="/testbed/database/records.db"
STATE_DIR="/testbed/state"
mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR"

echo "[preflight] checking database at ${DB} ..."

if python3 - "$DB" <<'PY'
import sqlite3, sys
db = sys.argv[1]
con = sqlite3.connect("file:%s?mode=ro" % db, uri=True)
try:
    n = con.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users").fetchone()[0]
finally:
    con.close()
print("[preflight] users table is readable: %d row(s)" % n)
PY
then
    status="ok"
    echo "OK: database readable"
else
    status="corrupted"
    echo "ERROR: database corrupted, cannot read"
fi

{
    echo "checked_at=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
    echo "database=${DB}"
    echo "status=${status}"
} > "${STATE_DIR}/preflight_done"

[ "$status" = "ok" ]
